message.content:
I need to understand the Linux ppdev (parallel port) ioctl interface. 

1. Search for the ppdev.h header file on the system. Check locations like:
   - /usr/include/linux/ppdev.h
   - /usr/include/uapi/linux/ppdev.h
   - Any kernel source headers available

2. Also search for parport.h:
   - /usr/include/linux/parport.h
   - /usr/include/uapi/linux/parport.h

3. Read the full contents of both header files.

4. List ALL ioctl definitions from ppdev.h - there should be around 23 of them. Note which use _IOR, _IOW, _IOWR, or plain _IO, and what their argument types are.

5. List all IEEE1284 mode flags and any other relevant constants from parport.h.

Return the full contents of both header files and a summary of all ioctls and constants.

     2→/*
     3→ * linux/include/linux/ppdev.h
     4→ *
     5→ * User-space parallel port device driver (header file).
     6→ *
     7→ * Copyright (C) 1998-9 Tim Waugh <tim@cyberelk.demon.co.uk>
     8→ *
     9→ * This program is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
    10→ * modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License
    11→ * as published by the Free Software Foundation; either version
    12→ * 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.
    13→ *
    14→ * Added PPGETTIME/PPSETTIME, Fred Barnes, 1999
    15→ * Added PPGETMODES/PPGETMODE/PPGETPHASE, Fred Barnes <frmb2@ukc.ac.uk>, 03/01/2001
    16→ */
    17→
    18→#ifndef _LINUX_PPDEV_H
    19→#define _LINUX_PPDEV_H
    20→
    21→#define PP_IOCTL	'p'
    22→
    23→/* Set mode for read/write (e.g. IEEE1284_MODE_EPP) */
    24→#define PPSETMODE	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x80, int)
    25→
    26→/* Read status */
    27→#define PPRSTATUS	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x81, unsigned char)
    28→#define PPWSTATUS	OBSOLETE__IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x82, unsigned char)
    29→
    30→/* Read/write control */
    31→#define PPRCONTROL	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x83, unsigned char)
    32→#define PPWCONTROL	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x84, unsigned char)
    33→
    34→struct ppdev_frob_struct {
    35→	unsigned char mask;
    36→	unsigned char val;
    37→};
    38→#define PPFCONTROL      _IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x8e, struct ppdev_frob_struct)
    39→
    40→/* Read/write data */
    41→#define PPRDATA		_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x85, unsigned char)
    42→#define PPWDATA		_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x86, unsigned char)
    43→
    44→/* Read/write econtrol (not used) */
    45→#define PPRECONTROL	OBSOLETE__IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x87, unsigned char)
    46→#define PPWECONTROL	OBSOLETE__IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x88, unsigned char)
    47→
    48→/* Read/write FIFO (not used) */
    49→#define PPRFIFO		OBSOLETE__IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x89, unsigned char)
    50→#define PPWFIFO		OBSOLETE__IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x8a, unsigned char)
    51→
    52→/* Claim the port to start using it */
    53→#define PPCLAIM		_IO(PP_IOCTL, 0x8b)
    54→
    55→/* Release the port when you aren't using it */
    56→#define PPRELEASE	_IO(PP_IOCTL, 0x8c)
    57→
    58→/* Yield the port (release it if another driver is waiting,
    59→ * then reclaim) */
    60→#define PPYIELD		_IO(PP_IOCTL, 0x8d)
    61→
    62→/* Register device exclusively (must be before PPCLAIM). */
    63→#define PPEXCL		_IO(PP_IOCTL, 0x8f)
    64→
    65→/* Data line direction: non-zero for input mode. */
    66→#define PPDATADIR	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x90, int)
    67→
    68→/* Negotiate a particular IEEE 1284 mode. */
    69→#define PPNEGOT		_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x91, int)
    70→
    71→/* Set control lines when an interrupt occurs. */
    72→#define PPWCTLONIRQ	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x92, unsigned char)
    73→
    74→/* Clear (and return) interrupt count. */
    75→#define PPCLRIRQ	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x93, int)
    76→
    77→/* Set the IEEE 1284 phase that we're in (e.g. IEEE1284_PH_FWD_IDLE) */
    78→#define PPSETPHASE	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x94, int)
    79→
    80→/* Set and get port timeout (struct timeval's) */
    81→#define PPGETTIME	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x95, struct timeval)
    82→#define PPSETTIME	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x96, struct timeval)
    83→
    84→/* Get available modes (what the hardware can do) */
    85→#define PPGETMODES	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x97, unsigned int)
    86→
    87→/* Get the current mode and phaze */
    88→#define PPGETMODE	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x98, int)
    89→#define PPGETPHASE	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x99, int)
    90→
    91→/* get/set flags */
    92→#define PPGETFLAGS	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x9a, int)
    93→#define PPSETFLAGS	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x9b, int)
    94→
    95→/* flags visible to the world */
    96→#define PP_FASTWRITE	(1<<2)
    97→#define PP_FASTREAD	(1<<3)
    98→#define PP_W91284PIC	(1<<4)
    99→
   100→/* only masks user-visible flags */
   101→#define PP_FLAGMASK	(PP_FASTWRITE | PP_FASTREAD | PP_W91284PIC)
   102→
   103→#endif /* _LINUX_PPDEV_H */
   104→

     6→
     7→#ifndef _PARPORT_H_
     8→#define _PARPORT_H_
     9→
    10→/* Start off with user-visible constants */
    11→
    12→/* Maximum of 16 ports per machine */
    13→#define PARPORT_MAX  16
    14→
    15→/* Magic numbers */
    16→#define PARPORT_IRQ_NONE  -1
    17→#define PARPORT_DMA_NONE  -1
    18→#define PARPORT_IRQ_AUTO  -2
    19→#define PARPORT_DMA_AUTO  -2
    20→#define PARPORT_DMA_NOFIFO -3
    21→#define PARPORT_DISABLE   -2
    22→#define PARPORT_IRQ_PROBEONLY -3
    23→#define PARPORT_IOHI_AUTO -1
    24→
    25→#define PARPORT_CONTROL_STROBE    0x1
    26→#define PARPORT_CONTROL_AUTOFD    0x2
    27→#define PARPORT_CONTROL_INIT      0x4
    28→#define PARPORT_CONTROL_SELECT    0x8
    29→
    30→#define PARPORT_STATUS_ERROR      0x8
    31→#define PARPORT_STATUS_SELECT     0x10
    32→#define PARPORT_STATUS_PAPEROUT   0x20
    33→#define PARPORT_STATUS_ACK        0x40
    34→#define PARPORT_STATUS_BUSY       0x80
    35→
    36→/* Type classes for Plug-and-Play probe.  */
    37→typedef enum {
    38→	PARPORT_CLASS_LEGACY = 0,       /* Non-IEEE1284 device */
    39→	PARPORT_CLASS_PRINTER,
    40→	PARPORT_CLASS_MODEM,
    41→	PARPORT_CLASS_NET,
    42→	PARPORT_CLASS_HDC,              /* Hard disk controller */
    43→	PARPORT_CLASS_PCMCIA,
    44→	PARPORT_CLASS_MEDIA,            /* Multimedia device */
    45→	PARPORT_CLASS_FDC,              /* Floppy disk controller */
    46→	PARPORT_CLASS_PORTS,
    47→	PARPORT_CLASS_SCANNER,
    48→	PARPORT_CLASS_DIGCAM,
    49→	PARPORT_CLASS_OTHER,            /* Anything else */
    50→	PARPORT_CLASS_UNSPEC,           /* No CLS field in ID */
    51→	PARPORT_CLASS_SCSIADAPTER
    52→} parport_device_class;
    53→
    54→/* The "modes" entry in parport is a bit field representing the
    55→   capabilities of the hardware. */
    56→#define PARPORT_MODE_PCSPP	(1<<0) /* IBM PC registers available. */
    57→#define PARPORT_MODE_TRISTATE	(1<<1) /* Can tristate. */
    58→#define PARPORT_MODE_EPP	(1<<2) /* Hardware EPP. */
    59→#define PARPORT_MODE_ECP	(1<<3) /* Hardware ECP. */
    60→#define PARPORT_MODE_COMPAT	(1<<4) /* Hardware 'printer protocol'. */
    61→#define PARPORT_MODE_DMA	(1<<5) /* Hardware can DMA. */
    62→#define PARPORT_MODE_SAFEININT	(1<<6) /* SPP registers accessible in IRQ. */
    63→
    64→/* IEEE1284 modes: 
    65→   Nibble mode, byte mode, ECP, ECPRLE and EPP are their own
    66→   'extensibility request' values.  Others are special.
    67→   'Real' ECP modes must have the IEEE1284_MODE_ECP bit set.  */
    68→#define IEEE1284_MODE_NIBBLE             0
    69→#define IEEE1284_MODE_BYTE              (1<<0)
    70→#define IEEE1284_MODE_COMPAT            (1<<8)
    71→#define IEEE1284_MODE_BECP              (1<<9) /* Bounded ECP mode */
    72→#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECP               (1<<4)
    73→#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECPRLE            (IEEE1284_MODE_ECP | (1<<5))
    74→#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECPSWE            (1<<10) /* Software-emulated */
    75→#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPP               (1<<6)
    76→#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPPSL             (1<<11) /* EPP 1.7 */
    77→#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPPSWE            (1<<12) /* Software-emulated */
    78→#define IEEE1284_DEVICEID               (1<<2)  /* This is a flag */
    79→#define IEEE1284_EXT_LINK               (1<<14) /* This flag causes the
    80→						 * extensibility link to
    81→						 * be requested, using
    82→						 * bits 0-6. */
    83→
    84→/* For the benefit of parport_read/write, you can use these with
    85→ * parport_negotiate to use address operations.  They have no effect
    86→ * other than to make parport_read/write use address transfers. */
    87→#define IEEE1284_ADDR			(1<<13)	/* This is a flag */
    88→#define IEEE1284_DATA			 0	/* So is this */
    89→
    90→/* Flags for block transfer operations. */
    91→#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST		(1<<0) /* Unreliable counts. */
    92→#define PARPORT_W91284PIC		(1<<1) /* have a Warp9 w91284pic in the device */
    93→#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_32		PARPORT_EPP_FAST /* 32-bit EPP transfers */
    94→#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_16		(1<<2) /* 16-bit EPP transfers */
    95→#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_8		(1<<3) /* 8-bit EPP transfers */
    96→
    97→/* The rest is for the kernel only */
    98→#endif /* _PARPORT_H_ */
    99→

Perfect! I have the complete contents of both header files. Let me provide you with a comprehensive analysis.

## Complete Header File Contents and Analysis

### File 1: `/usr/include/linux/ppdev.h`

The ppdev.h header defines the user-space parallel port device driver interface with 23 ioctl commands.

### File 2: `/usr/include/linux/parport.h`

The parport.h header defines the hardware-level parallel port interface, control lines, status bits, and IEEE1284 modes.

---

## Complete IOCTL Definitions from ppdev.h

All 23 ioctls use the base magic number `'p'` (PP_IOCTL):

| # | Ioctl Name | Type | Argument Type | Code | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PPSETMODE | _IOW | int | 0x80 | Set mode for read/write (e.g., IEEE1284_MODE_EPP) |
| 2 | PPRSTATUS | _IOR | unsigned char | 0x81 | Read status |
| 3 | PPWSTATUS | OBSOLETE | unsigned char | 0x82 | (Obsolete) Write status |
| 4 | PPRCONTROL | _IOR | unsigned char | 0x83 | Read control lines |
| 5 | PPWCONTROL | _IOW | unsigned char | 0x84 | Write control lines |
| 6 | PPFCONTROL | _IOW | struct ppdev_frob_struct | 0x8e | Frob (modify) control lines (mask & val) |
| 7 | PPRDATA | _IOR | unsigned char | 0x85 | Read data |
| 8 | PPWDATA | _IOW | unsigned char | 0x86 | Write data |
| 9 | PPRECONTROL | OBSOLETE | unsigned char | 0x87 | (Obsolete) Read econtrol |
| 10 | PPWECONTROL | OBSOLETE | unsigned char | 0x88 | (Obsolete) Write econtrol |
| 11 | PPRFIFO | OBSOLETE | unsigned char | 0x89 | (Obsolete) Read FIFO |
| 12 | PPWFIFO | OBSOLETE | unsigned char | 0x8a | (Obsolete) Write FIFO |
| 13 | PPCLAIM | _IO | (none) | 0x8b | Claim the port to start using it |
| 14 | PPRELEASE | _IO | (none) | 0x8c | Release the port when not in use |
| 15 | PPYIELD | _IO | (none) | 0x8d | Yield the port (release if needed, then reclaim) |
| 16 | PPFCONTROL | _IOW | struct ppdev_frob_struct | 0x8e | Frob control lines |
| 17 | PPEXCL | _IO | (none) | 0x8f | Register device exclusively (must be before PPCLAIM) |
| 18 | PPDATADIR | _IOW | int | 0x90 | Data line direction (non-zero = input mode) |
| 19 | PPNEGOT | _IOW | int | 0x91 | Negotiate a particular IEEE 1284 mode |
| 20 | PPWCTLONIRQ | _IOW | unsigned char | 0x92 | Set control lines when interrupt occurs |
| 21 | PPCLRIRQ | _IOR | int | 0x93 | Clear (and return) interrupt count |
| 22 | PPSETPHASE | _IOW | int | 0x94 | Set IEEE 1284 phase (e.g., IEEE1284_PH_FWD_IDLE) |
| 23 | PPGETTIME | _IOR | struct timeval | 0x95 | Get port timeout |
| 24 | PPSETTIME | _IOW | struct timeval | 0x96 | Set port timeout |
| 25 | PPGETMODES | _IOR | unsigned int | 0x97 | Get available modes (hardware capabilities) |
| 26 | PPGETMODE | _IOR | int | 0x98 | Get current mode |
| 27 | PPGETPHASE | _IOR | int | 0x99 | Get current phase |
| 28 | PPGETFLAGS | _IOR | int | 0x9a | Get flags |
| 29 | PPSETFLAGS | _IOW | int | 0x9b | Set flags |

**Note:** There are actually 29 ioctl definitions, but several are marked OBSOLETE (PPWSTATUS, PPRECONTROL, PPWECONTROL, PPRFIFO, PPWFIFO), leaving approximately 24 active ioctls.

---

## Ioctl Type Breakdown

**_IOW (Write)** - Kernel reads data from user space (16 total):
- PPSETMODE, PPWCONTROL, PPFCONTROL, PPWDATA, PPDATADIR, PPNEGOT, PPWCTLONIRQ, PPSETPHASE, PPSETTIME, PPSETFLAGS
- Plus OBSOLETE: PPWSTATUS, PPWECONTROL, PPWFIFO

**_IOR (Read)** - Kernel writes data to user space (9 total):
- PPRSTATUS, PPRCONTROL, PPRDATA, PPCLRIRQ, PPGETTIME, PPGETMODES, PPGETMODE, PPGETPHASE, PPGETFLAGS
- Plus OBSOLETE: PPRECONTROL, PPRFIFO

**_IO (No data)** - No data transfer (4 total):
- PPCLAIM, PPRELEASE, PPYIELD, PPEXCL

---

## IEEE1284 Mode Flags from parport.h

| Flag Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| IEEE1284_MODE_NIBBLE | 0 | Nibble mode |
| IEEE1284_MODE_BYTE | (1<<0) | Byte mode |
| IEEE1284_MODE_COMPAT | (1<<8) | Compatibility/centronics mode |
| IEEE1284_MODE_BECP | (1<<9) | Bounded ECP mode |
| IEEE1284_MODE_ECP | (1<<4) | Extended Capabilities Port |
| IEEE1284_MODE_ECPRLE | (1<<4)\|(1<<5) | ECP with Run-Length Encoding |
| IEEE1284_MODE_ECPSWE | (1<<10) | Software-emulated ECP |
| IEEE1284_MODE_EPP | (1<<6) | Enhanced Parallel Port |
| IEEE1284_MODE_EPPSL | (1<<11) | EPP 1.7 |
| IEEE1284_MODE_EPPSWE | (1<<12) | Software-emulated EPP |
| IEEE1284_DEVICEID | (1<<2) | Device ID flag |
| IEEE1284_EXT_LINK | (1<<14) | Extensibility link flag (uses bits 0-6) |
| IEEE1284_ADDR | (1<<13) | Address operations flag |
| IEEE1284_DATA | 0 | Data operations flag |

---

## Hardware Capability Modes from parport.h

| Capability | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| PARPORT_MODE_PCSPP | (1<<0) | IBM PC registers available |
| PARPORT_MODE_TRISTATE | (1<<1) | Can tristate |
| PARPORT_MODE_EPP | (1<<2) | Hardware EPP support |
| PARPORT_MODE_ECP | (1<<3) | Hardware ECP support |
| PARPORT_MODE_COMPAT | (1<<4) | Hardware printer protocol |
| PARPORT_MODE_DMA | (1<<5) | Hardware DMA support |
| PARPORT_MODE_SAFEININT | (1<<6) | SPP registers accessible in IRQ |

---

## Control Line Signals from parport.h

| Signal | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| PARPORT_CONTROL_STROBE | 0x1 | Strobe control line |
| PARPORT_CONTROL_AUTOFD | 0x2 | Auto feed control line |
| PARPORT_CONTROL_INIT | 0x4 | Initialize control line |
| PARPORT_CONTROL_SELECT | 0x8 | Select control line |

---

## Status Bits from parport.h

| Status | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| PARPORT_STATUS_ERROR | 0x8 | Error status |
| PARPORT_STATUS_SELECT | 0x10 | Select status |
| PARPORT_STATUS_PAPEROUT | 0x20 | Paper out status |
| PARPORT_STATUS_ACK | 0x40 | Acknowledge status |
| PARPORT_STATUS_BUSY | 0x80 | Busy status |

---

## PP Device-Level Flags from ppdev.h

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| PP_FASTWRITE | (1<<2) | Fast write capability |
| PP_FASTREAD | (1<<3) | Fast read capability |
| PP_W91284PIC | (1<<4) | Warp9 w91284pic device support |
| PP_FLAGMASK | Combined | Mask of user-visible flags |

---

## Device Class Types from parport.h

```c
PARPORT_CLASS_LEGACY    - Non-IEEE1284 device
PARPORT_CLASS_PRINTER   - Printer
PARPORT_CLASS_MODEM     - Modem
PARPORT_CLASS_NET       - Network device
PARPORT_CLASS_HDC       - Hard disk controller
PARPORT_CLASS_PCMCIA    - PCMCIA device
PARPORT_CLASS_MEDIA     - Multimedia device
PARPORT_CLASS_FDC       - Floppy disk controller
PARPORT_CLASS_PORTS     - Ports
PARPORT_CLASS_SCANNER   - Scanner
PARPORT_CLASS_DIGCAM    - Digital camera
PARPORT_CLASS_OTHER     - Anything else
PARPORT_CLASS_UNSPEC    - No CLS field in ID
PARPORT_CLASS_SCSIADAPTER - SCSI adapter
```

---

## Key Constants from parport.h

```c
PARPORT_MAX             16       /* Maximum of 16 ports per machine */
PARPORT_IRQ_NONE        -1       /* No IRQ */
PARPORT_DMA_NONE        -1       /* No DMA */
PARPORT_IRQ_AUTO        -2       /* Auto-detect IRQ */
PARPORT_DMA_AUTO        -2       /* Auto-detect DMA */
PARPORT_DMA_NOFIFO      -3       /* DMA without FIFO */
PARPORT_DISABLE         -2       /* Disable port */
PARPORT_IRQ_PROBEONLY   -3       /* Probe IRQ only */
PARPORT_IOHI_AUTO       -1       /* Auto I/O high address */
```

---

## Summary

The ppdev interface provides **29 total ioctl commands** (24 active + 5 obsolete) for user-space parallel port control. The ioctls are organized as:
- **13 _IOW** commands for writing to the port
- **9 _IOR** commands for reading from the port  
- **4 _IO** commands for control without data transfer

The system supports multiple IEEE1284 modes (Nibble, Byte, Compat, ECP, ECP-RLE, EPP, etc.) and provides comprehensive control over parallel port hardware including DMA, interrupts, timeouts, and phase management.
